newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer, Crystallex spar over Las Cristinas.
newsitem.headline: Placer, Crystallex spar over Las Cristinas.

text.p: Canadian junior miner Crystallex International Corp on Monday claimed rights to two blocks of gold heavyweight Placer Dome Inc's Las Cristinas property in Venezuela, but Placer said those claims were without foundation.

"Our ownership is secure," Placer spokesman Hugh Leggatt said of the Las Cristinas project. The company expects to begin mine construction within the next few months at the property, estimated to contain nine million ounces of gold reserves.

Crystallex said it acquired a Venezuelan company that long held rights to the disputed Las Cristinas blocks. Crystallex vice president Richard Marshall said the Venezuelan Supreme Court in October "ruled by final and binding decision that ownership rights of Cristinas four and six were held by the corporation we have just bought."
He declined to identify the Venezuelan company.

Marshall said Crystallex had held talks with Placer but declined to say if Crystallex was seeking to sell its rights to the disputed blocks to Placer. Crystallex was looking for potential partners to help develop the blocks, he said.

Crystallex's claims made investors nervous and called to mind recent ownership disputes involving Canadian companies over the vast mineral discoveries at Voisey's Bay in Newfoundland and Busang in Indonesia, analysts said.
"The whole situation is very unclear. It looks like it's going to be very, very complicated," said one analyst.
Placer's stock fell 1.25 to 28.10 in Toronto. Crystallex's shares rose 1.70 to 5.85 before retreating to 4.45 after Placer reiterated its view that its tenure remains secure.
For its part, Placer said Crystallex's account of the Supreme Court decision was completely false.
"The whole is not true. Our tenure is secure. It has been confirmed with the government. We are not in discussions with anybody over ownership," Leggatt said.

He said Placer was not interested in negotiating with Crystallex over its claims. The prior owner's rights to Las Cristinas were extinguished and the property reverted to the government in 1989, Placer said.

He said Placer expected to proceed with mine construction within months. The company has targeted May to start building. Placer has 70 percent of the property and Venezuelan state-owned Corporacion Venezolana de Guyana the rest.
Marshall said that blocks four and six of Las Cristinas hold a gold resource of about 13 million ounces. He said the bulk of the entire deposit appeared to reside on block four.
Leggatt disputed this but declined to be more specific.
Analysts believe Las Cristinas has the potential to host 15 million to 20 million ounces of gold.
